title: AI Agent book (English edition)
author: Bojie Li
what: The closest thing to a first-principles agents textbook: context, tools, memory, planning, multi-agent, evaluation.

title: 12-Factor Agents
author: HumanLayer (Dex Horthy)
what: Principles for production agents: own your prompts, own your context window, tools are structured output, small focused agents. Share-alike applies to quoted text.

title: Hugging Face Agents Course
author: Hugging Face
what: Unit 1 (what an agent is, the thought-action-observation loop), bonus units on fine-tuning for function calling and observability, unit 3 on agentic RAG.

title: Hugging Face MCP Course
author: Hugging Face
what: MCP architecture, building servers and clients, end to end.

title: Hugging Face LLM Course
author: Hugging Face
what: Chapter 1 (transformers), 6 (tokenizers, BPE from scratch), 11 (fine-tuning, LoRA), 12 (reasoning and GRPO).

title: Prompt Engineering Guide
author: DAIR.AI
what: A catalogue of prompting techniques with papers; read for breadth, not depth.

title: GraphRAG documentation
author: Microsoft
what: How GraphRAG builds entity graphs and community summaries, and global vs local search.

title: AI Agents for Beginners
author: Microsoft
what: Lessons on trustworthy agents, agents in production and agent security.

title: awesome-ai-engineer-interview
author: landedjobs
what: A question bank to drill against after the interview hub.

title: Foundations of Large Language Models
author: Tong Xiao and Jingbo Zhu
what: A free textbook on pretraining, generative models, prompting and alignment. Read the chapter that matches the section.

title: minbpe, nanoGPT and Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
author: Andrej Karpathy
what: Build a tokenizer and a GPT from scratch. The labs reuse the code ideas, not the videos.

title: Building effective agents; Effective context engineering; Contextual Retrieval
author: Anthropic Engineering
what: The canonical posts on workflow vs agent patterns, tool design, context engineering and contextual retrieval. Link only; summarised in our own words.

title: Evals FAQ and courses
author: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar
what: Error analysis first: trace review, open and axial coding, validating LLM judges. Link only.

title: AI Engineering
author: Chip Huyen
what: The best single book on the field. Chapter 6 is RAG and agents; chapters 3 and 4 are evaluation.

title: Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft)
author: Dan Jurafsky and James H. Martin
license: Free to read, no open licence
what: Tokenization, embeddings, language models and information retrieval from the textbook that defined them. Link only.

title: Simon Willison's weblog: prompt injection series
author: Simon Willison
what: Where the lethal trifecta and the dual-LLM pattern were named. Link only.
